item.title: Bodies of climbers who vanished 34 years ago found in Swiss Alps
item.description: The bodies of two climbers who disappeared in the Swiss Alps in 1992 have been found, freed from a melting glacier, police said.

item.title: Prosecutors say bullet engraving shows Charlie Kirk was shot over his politics
item.description: Prosecutors in Charlie Kirk 's killing pointed to an engraved bullet, arguing that its inscription shows Kirk was targeted for how the defendant perceived his politics.

item.title: Iran's top diplomat and Trump cast doubt on any hope for a peace deal
item.description: Iran's foreign minister says Tehran is interested only in a deal to fully end the war, not a ceasefire, after Trump says there's currently no dialogue at all.

item.title: Sen. Dan Sullivan, Mary Peltola advance in Alaska Senate primary
item.description: In Alaska, the top four vote getters in the primary advance to the general election.

item.title: Australian woman appeals murder convictions in poison mushroom case
item.description: Triple-murderer Erin Patterson appeals convictions for poisoning four of her estranged husband's relatives with death cap mushrooms.

item.title: Moving Through Grief
item.description: August is National Grief Awareness Month, and Kate Doerge wants to reimagine how we deal with grief. After the experience of losing her 16-year-old daughter, Kate decided it was time to reframe the feeling of sadness. We've all heard of the five stages of grief, but Kate suggests there are five actions to help you learn how to carry your grief. Plus, Norah talks about how she wants to be remembered, and Kate tells us how to show up for people who are grieving.

item.title: Harvard to pay $53 million after morgue manager sold body parts
item.description: Harvard University has agreed to pay $53 million to resolve lawsuits by families alleging it mishandled the bodies of loved ones donated to its medical school.

item.title: Skeletal remains believed to be ritual offering unearthed in Peru
item.description: The body was buried inside a canal, resting on its left flank, with the skull facing the pyramid and the Pacific Ocean, archaeologists said.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy said a voice ordered her to kill children, psychologist testifies
item.description: A psychologist who met with Lindsay Clancy in the hospital after her children's deaths testified Tuesday at her murder trial in Massachusetts.

item.title: Ebola Congo cases surpass 5,000 as record-setting pace of spread continues
item.description: The Ebola outbreak in Congo has passed 5,000 cases, government data showed, an unprecedented rate of spread that's outpacing efforts to slow it in one of the country's remotest regions.

item.title: Ukraine's fired defense minister calls for elections despite war with Russia
item.description: The former defense minister, whose firing sparked weeks of protests, said Ukraine needed to find a way to hold elections despite the prolonged war with Russia.

item.title: Trump says he paused 50% tariffs on some Canadian goods as deal being finalized
item.description: President Trump said Tuesday that the U.S. and Canada have reached a last-minute agreement to pause the 50% tariffs.

item.title: Byron Donalds, David Jolly to face off in Florida governor's race
item.description: Rep. Byron Donalds won the Republican primary for governor and former Rep. David Jolly won the Democratic primary, The Associated Press projects.

item.title: Florida Senate race set between Ashley Moody and Angie Nixon
item.description: GOP Sen. Ashley Moody and Democratic State Rep. Angie Nixon will face off in November after winning their primaries for U.S. Senate on Tuesday night, the Associated Press projects.

item.title: Oliver Gilbert wins Democratic primary for Florida's District 24
item.description: The heavily Democratic district includes predominantly Black and Hispanic communities in northern Miami-Dade and southern Broward counties.

item.title: Wasserman Schultz wins Democratic primary for Florida's District 20
item.description: The district includes predominantly Black communities in central and western Broward County.

item.title: U.S., South Korea cut short their joint military drills at Trump's direction
item.description: President Trump ordered the exercises be scaled back, citing what he said was a good relationship with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and South Korea's refusal to join the U.S. war against Iran.

item.title: Scandal-ridden Cory Mills ousted in GOP primary in Florida's 7th District
item.description: The Trump-backed incumbent has struggled to raise money for his reelection bid as the House Ethics Committee investigates numerous allegations against him.

item.title: Jared Moskowitz wins Democratic primary for Florida's District 25
item.description: The district that runs along part of Florida's southeast coast and includes portions of Palm Beach, Broward and Miami-Dade counties.

item.title: Watch: Lawyer hits car while trying to escape reporters outside courthouse
item.description: A lawyer attracted unwanted attention outside Boston Federal Court following Lawrence, Massachusetts, Mayor Brian DePeña's arraignment last Friday. The mayor's attorney rear-ended a parked vehicle while attempting to leave the area and remarked that he would bring bodyguards with him next time. Prosecutors allege DePeña improperly used more than $1.5 million in COVID small-business loans.

item.title: Crime in Washington, D.C., down to lowest level since 2010 since Trump's crackdown
item.description: A CBS News analysis finds crime in Washington, D.C., dropped to its lowest level since at least 2010 in the 12 months after President Trump declared a federal emergency and deployed the National Guard into the city. CBS News' Anna Schecter has more.

item.title: Oil prices rise to highest levels since July as Iran war continues
item.description: Oil prices on Tuesday reached their highest level since July as the war in Iran drags on without an end in site. CBS News national security analyst Aaron MacLean has more.

item.title: Justice Department to send record 1,000 monitors to polling places for midterm elections
item.description: The head of the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division announced Monday that she's planning to deploy 1,000 federal monitors to polling places throughout the U.S. for the midterm elections. Jen Fifield, reporter for ProPublica, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Trump says no talks with Iran planned as he posts map labeling Strait of Hormuz as U.S. territory
item.description: President Trump posted an image showing the Strait of Hormuz labeled as a U.S. territory on Tuesday. Mr. Trumps says no new talks with Iran are planned. CBS News' Nancy Cordes has more.

item.title: Panettiere was with on-and-off boyfriend when she died, police report says
item.description: Brian Hickerson and his brother, Zach, made the 911 call that brought first responders to the apartment where Hayden Panettiere was found unresponsive.

item.title: NASA images show 60-foot-wide crater on moon after SpaceX rocket booster crash
item.description: A NASA spacecraft circling the moon is providing the sharpest views yet of the crater carved by a crashing SpaceX rocket.

item.title: 8/18: CBS Evening News
item.description: New details in Hayden Panettiere's death; Recycling plant explosions kill 2 in Ohio.

item.title: Justice Department to send a record 1,000 monitors to midterm polling places
item.description: The Justice Department is planning to deploy a record 1,000 federal monitors to polling places throughout the U.S. for the midterm elections.

item.title: Beagles bred for research get new life amid questions over federal oversight
item.description: The USDA's own inspector general has repeatedly raised concerns about federal oversight of dog breeders.

item.title: State Farm is sending refund checks to customers. Here's who qualifies.
item.description: More than 7.2 million checks have been mailed so far, with millions more expected to go out this week, according to State Farm.
